title: Before you inject: LA safety card
topic: Eight medical conditions and drugs that change the local anesthetic or vasoconstrictor choice, as limit / avoid / OK pictograms.

claims.claim: Significant heart disease: LIMIT epinephrine to about 0.04 mg, about 2 cartridges of 1:100,000 (amber = limit; a cited convention; no time base on screen, 'per 30 min' in the caption)
claims.source: Becker DE & Reed KL, Anesth Prog 2012;59(2):90-101 (PMID 22822998; full text: 'most conservative and frequently cited' limit, reflects '30-minute time periods, not appointments'); cartridge arithmetic: Lignospan label (DailyMed) and Tolas AG et al., J Am Dent Assoc 1982;104:41-3 (PMID 6948029)

claims.claim: Non-selective beta-blocker: epinephrine is amber, not red: small doses, recheck BP before the next cartridge
claims.source: Hersh EV & Giannakopoulos H, Dent Clin North Am 2010;54(4):687-96 (PMID 20831932; abstract: epinephrine or levonordefrin with nonselective beta-blockers, dose related); Becker DE, Anesth Prog 2011;58(1):31-41 (PMID 21410363; full text: recheck HR/BP after each 20-40 mcg; not contraindicated); Becker & Reed 2012 (PMID 22822998)

claims.claim: Tricyclic antidepressant: epinephrine at low dose (amber); avoid levonordefrin (red; a label-level precaution, contested)
claims.source: Yagiela JA et al., Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol 1985;59(6):565-71 (PMID 3892411; dogs); Boakes AJ et al., Br Med J 1973;1(5849):311-5 (PMID 4685619; volunteers); mepivacaine-levonordefrin (Carbocaine) label; contested by Becker DE, Anesth Prog 2008;55(3):89-99 (PMID 18788844: 'not contraindicated ... used cautiously')

claims.claim: Recent cocaine use: no vasoconstrictor (epinephrine and levonordefrin both red; no hour figure)
claims.source: Yagiela JA, J Am Dent Assoc 1999;130(5):701-9 (PMID 10332135; abstract: cocaine intoxication); Brand HS et al., Br Dent J 2008;204(7):365-9 (PMID 18408681; abstract: postpone 6-24 h)

claims.claim: Uncontrolled hyperthyroidism: no vasoconstrictor (epinephrine and levonordefrin both red)
claims.source: Little JW, Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol Oral Radiol Endod 2006;101(3):276-84 (PMID 16504858; abstract: 'epinephrine or other pressor amines can cause a hypertensive crisis in the patient with uncontrolled hyperthyroidism'; 'avoid' is the conventional inference); interaction evidence rated weak by Yagiela 1999 (PMID 10332135)

claims.claim: Methemoglobinemia risk: avoid both prilocaine and benzocaine (red)
claims.source: Guay J, Anesth Analg 2009;108(3):837-45 (PMID 19224791; abstract); Citanest Plain Dental label (DailyMed: contraindicated in congenital or idiopathic methemoglobinemia); Trapp L & Will J, Dent Clin North Am 2010;54(4):665-75 (PMID 20831930)

claims.claim: Sulfite allergy: the vasoconstrictor cartridge carries sulfite (EPI cartridge with a SULFITE chip, red); use plain anesthetic (green)
claims.source: Naftalin LW & Yagiela JA, Dent Clin North Am 2002;46(4):733-46 (PMID 12436828; abstract); Becker & Reed 2012 (PMID 22822998; full text); Septocaine label (DailyMed)

claims.claim: Pregnancy: lidocaine with or without epinephrine is considered safe (LIDOCAINE and LIDO + EPI cartridges, both green)
claims.source: ACOG Committee Opinion No. 569, Obstet Gynecol 2013;122(2 Pt 1):417-22 (PMID 23969828; opinion PDF, marked 'Reaffirmed 2017'; later status not verified); ADA Oral Health Topic 'Pregnancy'; Hagai A et al., J Am Dent Assoc 2015;146(8):572-80 (PMID 26227642)

claims.claim: Fine print: conventional precautions, not trial-proven limits; check current references. Source line: Becker & Reed 2012, Yagiela 1999, Little 2006, Guay 2009, ACOG 2013
claims.source: Becker & Reed 2012 (PMID 22822998: maximum vasopressor doses not established); Guimaraes CC et al., BMJ Open 2021;11(7):e044357 (PMID 34266837: low to very low certainty)

claims.claim: Toy model / schematic: pictograms only (neutral cartridges with no color code, dashed 'about two' cartridge, BP gauge with repeat arrow, 'recent' clock, radiating thyroid, red drop turning brown, rash as a generic allergy symbol, SULFITE chip)
claims.source: Schematic; brown drop after Guay J, Anesth Analg 2009 (PMID 19224791): 'Chocolate-colored blood suggests methemoglobinemia but other colors may be found'

caption:
Before you inject: 8 histories that change the cartridge.

Heart disease: ~0.04 mg epi (~2 cartridges of 1:100,000) per 30 min is convention, not a proven cap.
Non-selective beta-blockers, tricyclics: epi isn't contraindicated; small doses, aspirate, recheck BP. Avoiding levonordefrin: label precaution.
Recent cocaine: defer elective care.
Pregnancy: lidocaine ± epi considered safe (ACOG).

Refs: Becker & Reed 2012, Becker 2008 & 2011 Anesth Prog; Hersh 2010, Naftalin 2002 DCNA; Yagiela 1985 OOOO; Yagiela 1999 JADA; Brand 2008 BDJ; Little 2006 OOOOE; Guay 2009 Anesth Analg; ACOG CO 569; FDA labels.
